metaData.originalTitle: Agentic Engineering 六条最佳实践
metaData.title: Six Best Practices for Agentic Engineering
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Starting from first principles and based on three axioms and five assumptions, this article systematically proposes six best practices for Agentic Engineering, aiming to deeply integrate AI Agents into the entire software engineering lifecycle to enhance R&D efficiency.
metaData.summary: This article presents a methodology for AI collaboration derived deductively from fundamental facts, with the core idea of treating AI Agents as deep collaborators in software engineering. The author first establishes three axioms: information loss in the intention-to-code chain, the essential characteristics of LLMs (context determines output, probabilistic output, limited working memory), and human cognition as a scarce resource. It then examines five common assumptions—such as feeding code to AI enables project understanding, or AI is unsuitable for complex systems—and points out their fallacies. Based on this, the article proposes six best practices: Context Engineering (Spec-First, Docs as Code, progressive disclosure), human-machine division of labor (Johari Window model), full-chain AI participation (from requirements to coding), small tasks with multi-layer validation, Knowledge as Code (encoding knowledge into structured Skills), and an Error-Driven feedback loop. Together, these practices form a comprehensive methodology for AI-assisted software development.

mainPoints.point: Software engineering is fundamentally an intention-to-code chain; AI changes the loss rate at each stage but does not eliminate the chain itself.
mainPoints.explanation: Every step in transforming vague intent into executable code incurs information loss. AI's role is to reduce loss at each stage, not to bypass the entire transformation process.

mainPoints.point: Context Engineering is the core practice, emphasizing Spec-First, Docs as Code, and progressive disclosure.
mainPoints.explanation: Maximize the quality of AI's understanding of project context by first producing a structured Spec to anchor intent, managing documentation and code in the same repository with version control, and loading context on demand rather than all at once.

mainPoints.point: Human-machine division of labor should follow the Johari Window model, achieving automation in the open area, knowledge injection in the blind area, AI supplementation in the potential area, and collaborative exploration in the unknown area.
mainPoints.explanation: Adopt different strategies based on the distribution of knowledge between humans and AI, optimizing the allocation of engineers' cognitive bandwidth. Let AI handle what it excels at, while humans focus on decision-making and review.

mainPoints.point: Small tasks combined with multi-layer validation are key to preventing the exponential accumulation of AI errors.
mainPoints.explanation: Tighter constraints and shorter step sizes reduce the likelihood of AI errors. Multi-layer validation—including Spec Review, Code Review, automated testing, and integration testing—aligns with the intention-to-code chain to ensure quality.

mainPoints.point: Knowledge as Code encodes team best practices into structured Skills, enabling version-controlled knowledge distribution.
mainPoints.explanation: Encode knowledge such as coding standards and design principles into AI-executable Skills, making AI a vehicle for knowledge distribution. Every team member automatically benefits from the team's best practices during collaboration.

keyQuotes: The essence of software engineering is to gradually refine the vague intent in the human mind into executable code through requirements → design → coding → testing. Each step incurs loss; AI changes the loss rate at each stage but does not eliminate the chain itself.
The bottleneck in the AI era is the upper limit of human review and decision-making bandwidth. The optimal strategy is to optimize the allocation of engineers' cognitive bandwidth.
It's not that AI isn't smart enough; it's that key knowledge hasn't been structured and provided to it.
Tighter constraints and shorter step sizes prevent the exponential accumulation of errors.

relatedArticles.title: From 7.9% to 54% Adoption: The Three-Stage Evolution of Kuaishou's Intelligent Code Review
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the three-generation architectural evolution of Kuaishou's intelligent code review system—from pure LLM heuristics to knowledge engine-driven, and finally to Agentic autonomous decision-making—increasing the CR adoption rate from 7.9% to 54%.

relatedArticles.title: Thinking About Agentic Engineering from First Principles
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically derives six core best practices for Agentic Engineering from first principles and introduces a modular, Skill-based open-source framework, aiming to combine engineering discipline with AI capabilities to reliably improve software engineering quality under complex constraints.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: You Don't Know Agent: Principles, Architecture and Engineering Practice - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically sorts out the core engineering practices of Agent architecture, covering key technical dimensions such as Agent Loop, Harness, context engineering, tool design, memory systems, multi-Agent organization, evaluation and tracing, and demonstrates the implementation of design principles through the OpenClaw open-source implementation.

relatedArticles.title: Beyond Cognitive Reconstruction: Stepping into the Engineering Revolution of Agentic Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the practical journey of Tencent engineers transitioning from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering, proposing an AI-assisted engineering system centered on context management and tool-oriented design.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: 5 Lessons Learned from 400 Million Tokens: What Happened When 6 AI Agents Wrote Code for 4 Days Straight?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through a four-day multi-agent automated programming experiment, this article reveals that 'glue code' and engineering stability are more challenging and critical than prompt design when building AI systems.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces the concept of AI Agent Skill, including its directory structure, writing standards, release process, and cross-platform challenges. It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.
